hints: Notice that $P$ points up and to the right while $Q$ points down and to the right, so their vertical parts oppose each other.
Think of placing the tail of $Q$ at the head of $P$ so the horizontal parts add and the vertical parts partly cancel.
Compare the four arrows for a long length to the right with only a small net vertical shift.
walkthrough: Identify the given vectors: $P$ is short and directed up-right, $Q$ is longer and directed down-right.
Use head-to-tail addition for $P + Q$: keep $P$ fixed, then place the tail of $Q$ at the arrow head of $P$.
Add components: both have rightward horizontal components so the resultant must have a large total length to the right.
Add components vertically: the upward part of $P$ and downward part of $Q$ are in opposite senses, so they largely cancel leaving only a small net vertical part.
The resultant from the tail of $P$ to the head of $Q$ is therefore long, to the right and almost horizontal.
